title: 11. Projects: Day 18 — Tool Ecosystems
summary: A LangChain create_tool_calling_agent equipped with seven @tool-decorated functions: list_inbox, read_email, mark_read, archive, reply, forward, create_task. Each tool mutates a shared mock inbox.
objectives: Build the Day 18 — Tool Ecosystems projects end to end
Keep a short README with assumptions and tradeoffs

sections.title: Project 1 — Inbox Zero Assistant (LangChain)
sections.body:
### Overview

A LangChain `create_tool_calling_agent` equipped with seven `@tool`-decorated functions: `list_inbox`, `read_email`, `mark_read`, `archive`, `reply`, `forward`, `create_task`. Each tool mutates a shared mock inbox. The `AgentExecutor` runs the agent up to `max_iterations=10` times. We seed the inbox with five realistic emails (urgent invoice, friendly coffee request, GitHub PR alert, newsletter, executive action item) and let the agent triage each one.

### Full Code

```python
"""
Inbox Zero Assistant — LangChain agent with 7 mock tools.
Run:  python day18_inbox_zero.py
"""
from typing import Optional

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain.agents import create_tool_calling_agent, AgentExecutor

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0.2)

# --- Mock inbox state -------------------------------------------------

INBOX: list[dict] = [
    {"id": "e1", "from": "alice@acme.com", "subject": "Late invoice #4421",
     "preview": "Our invoice is 14 days overdue. Please advise.",
     "read": False, "archived": False},
    {"id": "e2", "from": "bob@startup.io", "subject": "Coffee next week?",
     "preview": "Hey, want to grab coffee Tuesday? Long time no see.",
     "read": False, "archived": False},
    {"id": "e3", "from": "alerts@github.com", "subject": "PR #482 needs review",
     "preview": "sam opened PR #482: 'Refactor auth middleware'.",
     "read": False, "archived": False},
    {"id": "e4", "from": "newsletter@product.com", "subject": "Weekly digest",
     "preview": "Top stories this week: ...",
     "read": False, "archived": False},
    {"id": "e5", "from": "cto@acme.com", "subject": "Action required: Q3 OKR draft by EOD",
     "preview": "Please send me your team's Q3 OKRs by 6pm today.",
     "read": False, "archived": False},
]

TASKS: list[dict] = []
SENT_EMAILS: list[dict] = []

# --- Tools (each a mock with full type hints) -------------------------

@tool
def list_inbox() -> str:
    """List all unread, non-archived emails with id, from, subject, and read state."""
    rows = []
    for e in INBOX:
        if not e["archived"]:
            rows.append(f"[{e['id']}] from={e['from']} subject={e['subject']} read={e['read']}")
    return "\n".join(rows) if rows else "(inbox empty)"

@tool
def read_email(email_id: str) -> str:
    """Return the full preview text and metadata of an email by id. Marks it read."""
    for e in INBOX:
        if e["id"] == email_id:
            e["read"] = True
            return f"From: {e['from']}\nSubject: {e['subject']}\nPreview: {e['preview']}"
    return f"No email with id={email_id}"

@tool
def mark_read(email_id: str) -> str:
    """Mark an email as read without taking further action."""
    for e in INBOX:
        if e["id"] == email_id:
            e["read"] = True
            return f"Marked {email_id} as read."
    return f"No email with id={email_id}"

@tool
def archive(email_id: str) -> str:
    """Archive an email (removes it from the visible inbox)."""
    for e in INBOX:
        if e["id"] == email_id:
            e["archived"] = True
            return f"Archived {email_id}."
    return f"No email with id={email_id}"

@tool
def reply(email_id: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Send a reply to the sender of the given email."""
    target = next((e for e in INBOX if e["id"] == email_id), None)
    if not target:
        return f"No email with id={email_id}"
    SENT_EMAILS.append({
        "to": target["from"],
        "subject": f"Re: {target['subject']}",
        "body": body,
    })
    target["read"] = True
    return f"Sent reply to {target['from']} (re: {target['subject']})."

@tool
def forward(email_id: str, to_address: str) -> str:
    """Forward an email to another address."""
    target = next((e for e in INBOX if e["id"] == email_id), None)
    if not target:
        return f"No email with id={email_id}"
    SENT_EMAILS.append({
        "to": to_address,
        "subject": f"Fwd: {target['subject']}",
        "body": target["preview"],
    })
    return f"Forwarded {email_id} to {to_address}."

@tool
def create_task(email_id: str, task_description: str, due: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Create a follow-up task tied to an email. 'due' is an ISO date string or None."""
    target = next((e for e in INBOX if e["id"] == email_id), None)
    if not target:
        return f"No email with id={email_id}"
    TASKS.append({
        "email_id": email_id,
        "desc": task_description,
        "due": due,
    })
    return f"Created task: {task_description} (due={due}, src={email_id})."

tools = [list_inbox, read_email, mark_read, archive, reply, forward, create_task]

# --- Agent + executor -------------------------------------------------

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    ("system",
     "You are an inbox-zero assistant. For each email, decide ONE action: "
     "read it first if needed, then either reply, forward, archive, mark_read, "
     "or create_task. Process ALL unread emails in the inbox, then stop. "
     "Always start by calling list_inbox. Be terse in commentary. "
     "Newsletter emails should be archived. Urgent emails should be replied to "
     "or have a task created. PR alerts should be forwarded to the relevant team lead."),
    ("user", "{input}"),
    ("placeholder", "{agent_scratchpad}"),
])

agent = create_tool_calling_agent(llm, tools, prompt)
executor = AgentExecutor(
    agent=agent,
    tools=tools,
    verbose=True,
    max_iterations=10,
    handle_parsing_errors=True,
)

def print_final_state() -> None:
    print("\n=== SENT EMAILS ===")
    for e in SENT_EMAILS:
        print(f"  to={e['to']} subject={e['subject']} body={e['body'][:60]}...")
    print("\n=== TASKS ===")
    for t in TASKS:
        print(f"  {t}")
    print("\n=== INBOX (final) ===")
    for e in INBOX:
        print(f"  {e['id']} read={e['read']} archived={e['archived']} subject={e['subject']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    result = executor.invoke({
        "input": (
            "Process my inbox. For each unread email, take the most appropriate action. "
            "Reply to people who asked a question, create a task for action items due later, "
            "archive newsletters, forward PR alerts to lead@acme.com, mark read if no action needed."
        ),
    })
    print("\n=== AGENT OUTPUT ===")
    print(result["output"])
    print_final_state()
```

### Walkthrough

**`@tool` decorator with full type hints (lines 47-122).** LangChain's `@tool` reads the function signature, docstring, and type hints to build the JSON schema the LLM sees. The docstring is the model's only documentation — write it like a real API reference. Optional parameters (`due: Optional[str] = None`) become optional in the schema, so the model can omit them.

**Shared mutable state (lines 19-45).** `INBOX`, `TASKS`, and `SENT_EMAILS` are module-level lists that every tool mutates. This is fine for a single-process demo but breaks under concurrency. In production, wrap state in a class and pass via `RunnableConfig.configurable` or external storage (Redis, DB). The pattern of "tools mutate shared state" is the source of most agent bugs — make state changes explicit and logged.

**`create_tool_calling_agent` + `AgentExecutor` (lines 130-138).** The agent is the LLM-with-tools; the executor is the loop that runs the agent, dispatches tool calls, feeds results back, and stops when the agent emits no tool calls or hits `max_iterations`. `max_iterations=10` is a hard ceiling: with 5 emails and 2 tool calls each (read + action), the agent needs ~10 iterations. Set this too low and it gives up mid-triage.

**System prompt as policy (lines 124-129).** Notice the explicit rules: "Newsletter emails should be archived. Urgent emails should be replied to or have a task created." Without these, the agent will do reasonable but inconsistent things — sometimes replying to newsletters, sometimes archiving urgent items. Specific policy in the system prompt is the cheapest way to improve agent quality.

### Expected Output

```text
> Entering new AgentExecutor chain...
[list_inbox() -> 5 emails listed]
[read_email(e1) -> From: alice@acme.com... Late invoice #4421...]
[reply(e1, "Hi Alice, thanks for flagging...")]
[read_email(e2) -> From: bob@startup.io... Coffee next week?...]
[reply(e2, "Hey Bob, Tuesday works! How about 10am at the usual spot?")]
[read_email(e3) -> PR #482 needs review...]
[forward(e3, "lead@acme.com")]
[archive(e4)]
[read_email(e5) -> Q3 OKR draft by EOD...]
[create_task(e5, "Draft Q3 OKRs and send to cto@acme.com", "2025-01-17")]

=== AGENT OUTPUT ===
I processed all 5 emails in your inbox. Reply sent to Alice about the invoice;
reply sent to Bob confirming Tuesday coffee; PR #482 forwarded to lead@acme.com;
newsletter archived; task created for the Q3 OKR draft due today.

=== SENT EMAILS ===
  to=alice@acme.com subject=Re: Late invoice #4421 body=Hi Alice, thanks for flagging. I'm checking with finance...
  to=bob@startup.io subject=Re: Coffee next week? body=Hey Bob, Tuesday works! How about 10am at the usual spot?
  to=lead@acme.com subject=Fwd: PR #482 needs review body=PR #482 needs review...

=== TASKS ===
  {'email_id': 'e5', 'desc': "Draft Q3 OKRs and send to cto@acme.com", 'due': '2025-01-17'}

=== INBOX (final) ===
  e1 read=True archived=False subject=Late invoice #4421
  e2 read=True archived=False subject=Coffee next week?
  e3 read=False archived=False subject=PR #482 needs review
  e4 read=False archived=True subject=Weekly digest
  e5 read=True archived=False subject=Action required: Q3 OKR draft by EOD
```

sections.title: Project 2 — Multi-doc Summarizer (Pydantic AI)
sections.body:
### Overview

A single Pydantic AI agent has four tools: `list_docs`, `read_doc(name)`, `summarize_doc(name)` (which internally calls a *nested* LLM agent to produce the summary), and `merge_summaries(summaries)` (which calls *another* nested LLM to extract cross-cutting themes). This is the **nested-agent** pattern: tools that look like simple functions from the outer agent's perspective but actually run their own LLM calls underneath. The outer agent's intelligence is in orchestration ("summarize every doc, then merge"); the nested agents handle the language-heavy work.

### Full Code

```python
"""
Multi-doc Summarizer — Pydantic AI agent with tools that call nested LLMs.
Run:  python day18_multi_doc_summarizer.py
"""
from typing import List

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent

# --- Mock doc store ---------------------------------------------------

DOCS: dict[str, str] = {
    "q3-okrs.md": (
        "# Q3 OKRs\n"
        "Objective 1: Launch v2 API with 99.9% uptime.\n"
        "Objective 2: Reduce p95 latency to 200ms.\n"
        "Objective 3: Onboard 3 enterprise customers."
    ),
    "incident-postmortem-0115.md": (
        "# Postmortem: Auth Outage 2025-01-15\n"
        "Root cause: misconfigured rate limiter rejected valid tokens.\n"
        "Duration: 47 minutes. Affected 12% of users.\n"
        "Action items: add canary deploy, fix rate limiter config, add alerting."
    ),
    "customer-feedback-jan.md": (
        "# January Customer Feedback\n"
        "Top praise: new dashboard UI is much cleaner.\n"
        "Top complaints: export to CSV is slow, mobile layout broken on iOS.\n"
        "Net sentiment: +18 (up from +9 last month)."
    ),
    "team-retro-notes.md": (
        "# Retro 2025-01-17\n"
        "Went well: faster deploys, better on-call rotation.\n"
        "Didn't go well: too many meetings, planning fell behind.\n"
        "Actions: meeting-free Wednesdays, hire 1 backend eng."
    ),
}

# --- Output types -----------------------------------------------------

class DocSummary(BaseModel):
    name: str
    summary: str
    key_points: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

class Themes(BaseModel):
    themes: List[str] = Field(description="3-5 cross-cutting themes across documents")

# --- Nested agents (used INSIDE tools) --------------------------------

chunk_summarizer = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    output_type=DocSummary,
    system_prompt=(
        "Summarize a single document. Keep summary under 60 words. "
        "Extract 2-4 key points as short bullets (<15 words each). "
        "Set 'name' to the document's filename."
    ),
)

theme_extractor = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    output_type=Themes,
    system_prompt=(
        "Given document summaries and key points, extract 3-5 cross-cutting themes "
        "that appear across multiple documents. Return as a list of short phrases "
        "(<10 words each)."
    ),
)

# --- Outer agent + tools ----------------------------------------------

summarizer = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt=(
        "You produce a merged report across multiple documents. Workflow: "
        "(1) call list_docs, "
        "(2) call summarize_doc for EACH document, "
        "(3) call merge_summaries with all summaries, "
        "(4) return the merged report text as your final response. "
        "Do not skip documents."
    ),
)

@summarizer.tool_plain
def list_docs() -> List[str]:
    """List all available document names."""
    return list(DOCS.keys())

@summarizer.tool_plain
def read_doc(name: str) -> str:
    """Return the full text of a document by name."""
    return DOCS.get(name, f"ERROR: no document named {name!r}")

@summarizer.tool_plain
def summarize_doc(name: str) -> DocSummary:
    """Summarize a document. Internally calls a nested summarizer LLM agent."""
    text = DOCS.get(name)
    if text is None:
        return DocSummary(name=name, summary=f"ERROR: no document named {name!r}", key_points=[])
    # Nested agent call — costs one extra LLM call per doc.
    prompt = f"Document name: {name}\n\nDocument text:\n{text}\n\nSummary:"
    result = chunk_summarizer.run_sync(prompt)
    return result.output

@summarizer.tool_plain
def merge_summaries(summaries: List[DocSummary]) -> str:
    """Merge per-doc summaries into a final report. Calls a nested LLM for themes."""
    overview = "\n".join(f"- {s.name}: {s.summary}" for s in summaries)
    themes_input = "\n".join(f"- {s.name}: {'; '.join(s.key_points)}" for s in summaries)
    themes_result = theme_extractor.run_sync(
        f"Document summaries and key points:\n{themes_input}\n\nCross-cutting themes:"
    )
    themes = themes_result.output.themes
    return (
        f"# Merged Document Report\n\n"
        f"## Per-document summaries\n{overview}\n\n"
        f"## Cross-cutting themes\n" + "\n".join(f"- {t}" for t in themes)
    )

# --- Run --------------------------------------------------------------

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("[run] summarizing all docs...")
    result = summarizer.run_sync("Summarize all available documents and merge them.")
    print("\n=== MERGED REPORT ===")
    print(result.output)
```

### Walkthrough

**Nested agents inside tools (lines 60-101).** `summarize_doc` is a tool from the outer agent's perspective, but internally it calls `chunk_summarizer.run_sync(prompt)`, which is a full LLM agent invocation. Same for `merge_summaries` calling `theme_extractor`. The outer agent sees tools as opaque functions; it does not know or care that they invoke LLMs. This is the cleanest way to compose specialized agents.

**`tool_plain` vs `tool` (lines 84, 90, 98, 113).** Use `@agent.tool_plain` when the tool does not need the run context (no deps, no access to usage stats). Use `@agent.tool` when you need `ctx.deps` or `ctx.usage`. The first parameter of `tool_plain` is a real parameter the LLM must supply; the first parameter of `tool` is the context and is invisible to the LLM.

**Cost awareness (line 100).** Every `summarize_doc` call is one LLM invocation. With 4 documents, that is 4 nested calls plus 1 outer call plus 1 theme-extractor call = 6 LLM calls total. For 100 documents, that is 102 calls — watch your bill. Batch summarization (one LLM call for multiple docs) is cheaper but lower quality. The nested pattern trades cost for specialization.

**Why not just one big agent?** You could give the outer agent all 4 documents in one prompt and ask for a merged summary. That works for 4 short docs. It fails for 40 long docs (context overflow) and produces lower-quality summaries (the model rushes). The nested pattern scales: each doc gets focused attention from a specialized summarizer, then a synthesizer combines the focused outputs.

### Expected Output

```text
[run] summarizing all docs...

=== MERGED REPORT ===
# Merged Document Report

## Per-document summaries
- q3-okrs.md: Q3 goals focus on API reliability (99.9% uptime), latency (p95 < 200ms), and onboarding 3 enterprise customers.
- incident-postmortem-0115.md: 47-minute auth outage on Jan 15 caused by misconfigured rate limiter; affected 12% of users; canary deploys and alerting added.
- customer-feedback-jan.md: January sentiment up to +18 from +9; dashboard UI praised; CSV export and iOS layout need fixes.
- team-retro-notes.md: Faster deploys and on-call rotation went well; too many meetings and lagging planning are concerns; hiring 1 backend eng.

## Cross-cutting themes
- Reliability and uptime are recurring priorities across OKRs and incident response
- Customer experience issues (slow export, mobile layout) need engineering attention
- Process improvements (canary deploys, meeting-free days) being applied after retro
- Hiring and team capacity are constraints on Q3 goals
```
